name: The Gologorica–Gračišće line
route: Gologorica and Gračišće → Poreč, Crikvenica → United States, South Africa, Australia
note: David's line, and the one Carlo and Camillo belong to. It is also the line whose emigrant spelling became Defranceski — a form now concentrated in South Africa.

name: The Carnia line
note: No longer a guess about weavers in general. A De Franceschi of Mione is named on the 1679 headmen's list as working in the Habsburg County of Pazin — the same county the family's Istrian villages sit in. The route is documented; the descent is not.

name: The Pazin-county line
note: Treated as unrelated to the Carnia line by the existing research. That is an inference from an absent record, and it is challengeable.

name: The Domenico line
note: Municipal councillors by 1655, then lawyers and officials. Sparse.

name: The Svetvinčenat line — the castle the name never left
earliest: Elena di Franceschi, baptised at Svetvinčenat, 21 December 1628
route: Carnia (inferred) → Svetvinčenat / San Vincenti, continuously 1628–1791 — with daughters marrying out to Albona, Parenzo and Vodnjan, and sons staying
note:
**Split out of [the Ližnjan line](/lines/) on 28 September 2026, and not because it got big.**

*The castle was the Ližnjan line's **first stop** and its **earliest entry** — «Elena di Franceschi, Svetvinčenat, 21 December 1628». **Leaving it there asserted a descent nobody has proved.*** This archive's own worklist says of Svetvinčenat that *«whether it is a branch, the parent stock, or an unrelated household of the name is exactly the question a one-name study exists to ask»*. **A line that runs «Svetvinčenat → Fažana → Ližnjan» answers that question by drawing it.**

**What stands here on its own feet.** *Read page by page off three films — **005497884** (1666–1707), **005497885** (births 1709–1764) and **005497886** (marriages from 1762):* **158 people**, **nine households**, **1628 to 1791**, and the fifteen years 1738–1752 that no index reaches walked frame by frame.

**Four households baptising at once in the 1740s** — *[Jacobo × Pascasia](/person/pascasia-de-franceschi-later-calluzzi-fl-1743-1765-c1720/), [Matteo × Francisca](/person/francisca-de-franceschi-wife-of-matteo-fl-1741-1752-c1718/), [Pietro × Jacoba](/person/jacoba-giacoma-de-franceschi-fl-1738-1743-c1715/), [Vittorio × Dominica](/person/dominica-de-franceschi-wife-of-vittorio-fl-1745-1749-c1720/)* — **with [Gasparo × Maria](/person/maria-de-franceschi-wife-of-gasparo-fl-1744-1773-c1720/) beside them.** *None of them is in any index anywhere.*

**And the marriages show the shape of the place.** *The daughters married **out** and the husbands came **in** — Elena to a Santalezza of the Albona territory in 1766, [Fusca](/person/fusca-de-franceschi-m-1773-c1755/) to a Jacomini of Parenzo in 1773, and a Corva «dà Cargna» marrying into the castle in 1774.* **The sons stayed.**

**⚠ Its origin is inferred, not documented.** *This archive argues the castle **is the Carnian colony** — the godparent circle around the 1660s baptisms is Carnian, and Kandler lists the Carnian families settled at Sanvincenti. **That is why «origin: Carnia» is set here** — but it is an inference from company kept, not a document of arrival, and it is why this line hangs off [the Carnia line](/lines/) rather than standing as a fifth origin of its own.*

**⚠ And its relationship to Ližnjan is now an open question rather than a drawn line.** *The two may be one stock, or the castle may be the parent of the southern-Istrian group, or they may be unrelated households of a common name.* **The archive does not know, and the diagram no longer pretends otherwise.**

name: The Ližnjan line
earliest: Elena di Franceschi, Svetvinčenat, 21 December 1628 — **but see the caution below**
route: Svetvinčenat and Pula → Fažana, Premantura, Barban → Ližnjan → United States, Germany, France
note:
**⚠ Its head was split off on 28 September 2026.** *This line began at **Svetvinčenat** and ran «Svetvinčenat and Pula → Fažana → Ližnjan». **The castle now has **a line of its own, above****, because keeping it here asserted a descent this archive has never proved — and the castle's own record (158 people, nine households, 1628–1791) is far larger than anything downstream of it.* **The route below is kept because the southern-Istrian material genuinely runs through those places**; what is withdrawn is the claim that the Svetvinčenat households of the 1600s and 1700s are its ancestors. *(open.)*

**No longer lore.** This row used to read «from the existing family research; no register work done yet», and that has not been true since the southern-Istrian node was read out in full and, on 21 September 2026, the **Svetvinčenat marriage register 1762–1815** was opened for the first time — a volume FamilySearch has never indexed. The cluster now stands at fifteen documented households from 1628, with a first father-and-son pair — *«Victorio de Franceschi filio Antonij»*, 4 February 1773. **It is still not a descent.** Every household is drawn as its own node and joined to no other, because the 1623–1762 gap in the marriage book is exactly where the joins would be.

**28 September 2026 — a working man on this line's own ground, found by a diacritic.** *«Pučki prijatelj» (Krk) prints two subscription lists: **19 December 1919**, collected «među radnicima u **arsenalu**» — among the workers of the **Pula arsenal** — giving «**Defrančeski Antun**»; and **27 February 1920**, «Sabrano u **Ližnjanu** kod Pule», giving «**Defrančeski Ante**».* **[He has a page](/person/ante-antun-defranceski-of-liznjan-fl-1919-1920-c1885/)** — *and no earlier sweep found him, because this archive had searched «Defranceschi» and «Defranceski» and never **«Defrančeski»**, the form a Croatian paper actually prints.* **One diacritic, and an arsenal worker at Ližnjan was invisible.**

name: The Dalmatian line — Omiš and Imotski
route: Zadar (14c–16c) → Omiš → Imotski and Perinuša (1717) → Split
note: Almost certainly not your family, and now the best-documented line in the archive after Gologorica. A family chart carries it through twenty generations from a Niccolò of 1318 — four generations holding Zadar offices, a notary, a municipal archivist and an officer of the port salt-house, then Omiš from the later 1500s. Gasparo the admiral (1562–1609) and Giovanni il Zuane (1673–1741), who took Imotski in 1717, are both on it with dates that match the independent sources exactly. Their prefix was removed by Napoleonic decree, so they are Franceschi today — about 60 in Croatia, 25 of them in Split.

name: The Vodnjan line
earliest: Pietro, standing behind a marriage of the 1770s
route: Vodnjan (Dignano), southern Istria — with weddings at Šišan and Svetvinčenat, and a death at Rovinj in 1728
note: Found in the 1945 cadastre, then opened properly on 9 September 2026 by reading the parish books. The baptism register gives eight households 1816–1865; the marriage register — **which FamilySearch has never indexed** — was read opening by opening and produced the line itself. **Five generations**, from a Pietro who stands behind a marriage of the 1770s, through Gio. Maria De Franceschi and Michiela Zambaletta, to their children Pietro, Cristoforo and Veniera and their grandchildren married off in the 1820s. A second, separate line runs from a Domenico. At least four De Franceschi women married out of the name before the register opens. And a household of three brothers — **Don Stefano the priest, Pietro the ploughman and Cristoforo the weaver, all «di Giuseppe»** — in which the priest witnessed sixteen weddings while his brothers signed with a cross. No longer the newest open question; now the best-documented cluster in southern Istria.

name: The Seget line — Umag
route: Crete (Candia) → Istria after 1669 → Umag and Seget → Brtonigla, Koper
note: A noble house that fled Crete when the Ottomans took it in 1669, bought the Seget estate from the Venier in 1720 and were made citizens of Umag in 1730. Marc'Antonio (1671–1758) was a physician married to a Greek wife, Crissulla Marulli; his son Alvise served as dragoman at the Ottoman Porte. Published scholarship treats them and the Gologorica family as the two Istrian branches of one family — which, if it holds, is the largest single claim anyone has made about this surname in Istria.
